draft.title: Cells as the building blocks of life
card: All living things are made of one or more cells. A cell is the smallest unit that can carry out the processes of life, such as growing and using energy.
made of one cell only, such as an amoeba. That single cell carries out every process the organism needs.
made of many cells, such as a tree or a human. Cells work together to keep the whole organism alive.
Most cells are too small to see with the naked eye. We use a microscope to see them.
draft.remember: Cells are the smallest units of life, and an organism may have one cell or many.

a.q: Why is a cell called a building block of life?
opts: All living things are made of one or more cells
Only large living things are made of cells
Cells are found only in animals and plants
Cells are the smallest things that exist
a.why: All living things are made of cells, and a cell is the smallest unit that carries out the processes of life. Cells are not the smallest things that exist, because the card only says they are the smallest units of life.
a.clue: Think about what every living thing has in common.

b.q: A scientist views a drop of pond water under a microscope and sees one tiny organism. It grows and uses energy, and it has only one cell. What can be concluded?
opts: It is alive, because one cell can carry out life processes
It is not alive, because living things need many cells
It is alive only if it is part of a larger organism
It is not alive, because it is too small to see by eye
b.why: A single cell can carry out the processes of life, so a unicellular organism is a complete living thing. Being too small to see does not decide whether something is alive, since most cells are only visible with a microscope.
b.clue: Can a living thing be made of just one cell?

a.best: All living things are made of one or more cells

b.best: It is alive, because one cell can carry out life processes
